sources.title: Texas Education Code §§ 25.085–25.086 — Compulsory Attendance and Exemptions
sources.notes: Primary statutory source for compulsory-attendance ages and the private/parochial-school good-citizenship exemption used in Texas home-school law.

sources.title: Home Schooling
sources.notes: TEA states that it does not regulate, index, monitor, approve, register, or accredit home-school programs and summarizes the Leeper framework.

sources.title: Home Schools — Commissioner Correspondence
sources.notes: Agency guidance on withdrawal documentation, letters of assurance, and the basic education goals described for a home-school curriculum.

requirements.summary: Texas compulsory attendance generally applies beginning at age 6, or earlier in specified enrollment circumstances, until the child reaches the 19th birthday, unless a statutory exemption applies. A child attending a qualifying private or parochial school that includes a study of good citizenship is exempt, and Texas home schools operate within the private-school exemption recognized by Leeper.
requirements.appliesWhen: The child is within the compulsory-attendance range and the family is relying on the Texas home-school/private-school exemption.
requirements.notes: The dashboard should present the exemption and age rule together rather than imply home-schooled students must attend a public school.

requirements.summary: The Texas Education Agency does not register home-school programs. TEA states that it does not regulate, index, monitor, approve, register, or accredit programs chosen by parents for home schooling.
requirements.appliesWhen: A family is operating a Texas home school and is asking whether annual registration with TEA is required.
requirements.notes: This does not eliminate separate withdrawal or local assurance interactions when applicable.

requirements.summary: When a student is leaving a Texas public school to be home schooled, TEA guidance states that a signed and dated parent or guardian notice or withdrawal form stating that the student is being home schooled and the date home schooling began is sufficient documentation for disenrollment.
requirements.appliesWhen: The student is currently enrolled in a Texas public school and the family is withdrawing the student to begin home schooling.
requirements.notes: TEA guidance says personal appearance, curriculum review, or additional withdrawal requirements are not necessary for successful withdrawal.

requirements.summary: A public school district that becomes aware of a student who may be home schooled may request a written letter of assurance from the parents. TEA guidance states that such a letter is not required each year.
requirements.appliesWhen: A Texas public school district requests assurance that a student is being home schooled.

requirements.summary: TEA's current home-school guidance states that the course of study must include good citizenship. TEA's commissioner correspondence describes the home-school curriculum as designed to meet basic education goals including reading, spelling, grammar, mathematics, and a study of good citizenship.
requirements.appliesWhen: The family is operating a bona fide Texas home school under the Leeper/private-school framework.
requirements.notes: The ruleset preserves both the statutory good-citizenship language and TEA's broader Leeper-based curriculum description for human review.

requirements.summary: No statewide home-school portfolio requirement is asserted by this ruleset because the official sources reviewed for this version do not establish one.
requirements.appliesWhen: Any Texas home-school family using Khaemenes compliance-support records.
requirements.notes: Khaemenes may recommend educational portfolios, transcripts, and work samples without labeling them as Texas legal requirements.

requirements.summary: This research version does not assert a statewide annual home-school testing or evaluation mandate because the official sources reviewed here do not establish one.
requirements.appliesWhen: Any Texas home-school family using Khaemenes compliance-support records.
requirements.notes: Remain unknown until human review confirms whether any additional current authority should be represented.

legalBoundary: Compliance-support only; not legal advice, legal certification, or a government filing. Human administrative review is required before this ruleset is marked verified.
